decision: Grant Harrow Industrial exclusive US distribution of our sensor module for 3 years

framing.context: Harrow Industrial reaches every buyer in our category and is offering exclusive US distribution for 3 years. Harrow also owns Meridian, a house-brand sensor line that competes with ours in the same catalog slot. The draft agreement has no minimum purchase commitment, no marketing spend commitment, and no performance-based termination right for us; it is terminable by Harrow on 60 days notice. Our direct sales are $1.1M ARR from 14 accounts, growing 8% per quarter. Harrow projects $6M in year two but will not put any of it in the contract.
options: Counter: non-exclusive, or exclusive with a $2M/yr minimum and a 12-month performance termination right
Stay direct and hire two field sales reps

members.name: Founder
members.decisive_reason: A projection they will not sign is not a commitment.

answers.P1_timing: Their quarter ends 2019-11-30. That is their deadline, not ours.
answers.P2_reversibility: 1-way. We would dismantle direct sales and could not rebuild those 14 relationships quickly.
answers.P3_expected_value: If Harrow performs, $6M. If they shelve us, we lose the $1.1M we already have.
answers.P4_downside_cap: Losing direct revenue is company-ending inside 9 months.
answers.P5_opportunity_cost: Exclusivity forecloses every other channel for 3 years.
answers.P6_information: Will Harrow accept a minimum purchase commitment? One ask answers it.
answers.P7_second_order: Once we are exclusive, Harrow controls our pricing and our customer relationships.
answers.P8_strategy_fit: Distribution reach fits. Losing the customer relationship does not.
answers.P10_kill_criteria: No stated exit if they underperform. That is the problem.

members.name: VP Sales
members.decisive_reason: We cannot build national coverage on 14 accounts and two reps.

answers.P1_timing: Sign before their fiscal year closes or lose the slot.
answers.P4_downside_cap: We keep the product; worst case we go direct again.
answers.P5_opportunity_cost: Two field reps cost $500k and take a year to ramp.
answers.P7_second_order: Harrow's brand legitimises us with procurement teams.

known_good.recommendation_class: NO-GO on the exclusive as drafted; counter to non-exclusive or exclusivity conditioned on a minimum purchase commitment and a performance termination right
known_good.decisive_fact: Harrow owns a competing house brand (Meridian) in the same catalog slot and has committed to nothing: no minimum purchase, no marketing spend, and unilateral 60-day termination. Exclusivity is therefore a free option for Harrow and a one-way surrender of the only channel the company controls. The $6M projection has no contractual force.
known_good.what_actually_happened: Companies that signed this structure were listed but never pushed; Harrow's sales force defaulted to the house brand, orders came in at roughly 15% of projection, and the startup had by then dismantled direct sales and could not rebuild the 14 accounts inside its runway.
known_good.why_it_was_right: The correct move is to make exclusivity cost Harrow something. Either they commit volume, or they get non-exclusive access. Both preserve the direct channel while testing whether Harrow's interest is real.
